title: Power BI
seoTitle: Power BI Consultant & Dashboard Development | EfiOps
metaDescription: Power BI dashboards, data models and reporting improvements for clearer business decisions. Work directly with a Maidstone-based operations and data specialist.
eyebrow: Power BI · Clarity from your data
lead: When every number needs an explanation, a dashboard should help you find it. Bring sales, costs, capacity and performance into a reporting view that tells your team where to look next.

sections.heading: The report should explain the work, not add to it.
paragraphs: If every meeting starts with rebuilding a spreadsheet, the reporting process needs attention. If two reports show different totals, the definitions need attention. And if a dashboard looks impressive but nobody acts on it, the questions need attention.
We start with what you need to know: what changed, where performance differs, what is causing the difference and what should happen next.

sections.heading: From raw records to a useful reporting view.
items: Data preparation and modelling. Organise source data, relationships and calculations around consistent definitions.
Dashboard design. Build clear views of the measures that matter, with filters and comparisons that help people investigate.
Existing report improvements. Review confusing visuals, unreliable measures, slow models and repetitive preparation.
Operational reporting. Explore forecasts, capacity, staffing, production performance, quality checks and other business measures.
Refresh and handover. Plan how data reaches the report, how access works and how the team maintains it.

sections.heading: A reporting project starts with a question.
paragraphs: We agree the decisions the report should support, inspect the available data and define the measures. A first reporting view is then checked against known records before the layout and interactions are refined.
The handover explains the definitions, source limitations and refresh process. Microsoft licensing and sharing requirements are reviewed as part of the scope.

faqs.question: Can you improve an existing Power BI report?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can review its model, calculations, usability and refresh process, then agree which changes will be most useful.

faqs.question: Can you work with SQL and spreadsheets?
faqs.answer: Yes. Those are familiar starting points. The exact connection and refresh approach depends on where the data lives and how access is provided.

faqs.question: What if our data is inconsistent?
faqs.answer: We identify the gaps before presenting the report as dependable. Some projects need source cleanup or clearer definitions before dashboard development.

faqs.question: Will the dashboard replace our planning application?
faqs.answer: A dashboard is designed to analyse information. If your team needs to enter plans, assign work or manage records, a custom business application may be the better fit.

cta.label: Discuss your reporting
cta.heading: What would you like your reporting to explain?
cta.text: Tell us which questions are difficult to answer and where the data currently lives.

primaryIntent: Power BI consultant; Power BI dashboard development.
summary: Turn scattered records into useful answers, with measures your team can trust.

useCases.title: Which channel is actually making money?
useCases.body: Put sales beside costs and returns. Compare online and in-store performance without confusing revenue with profit.

useCases.title: Can we deliver next week’s plan?
useCases.body: Bring orders, staffing and capacity into one view. Spot a busy day before it becomes a missed commitment.

useCases.title: Why is the headline number different?
useCases.body: Agree the definitions behind each measure, trace the source and investigate differences instead of debating spreadsheets.

journey.heading: From separate exports to a margin you can explain.
journey.example: A retailer wants to compare online and in-store margin.
journey.question: Which channel is making money?
scope: Revenue and direct costs by channel
journey.boundary: Stock valuation and cash-flow forecasting are separate questions.

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Follow the number back to its source.
stages.body: We inspect order exports, cost records and the report you use today. We agree how returns, dates and channel names are recorded before deciding which measures belong in the dashboard.
stages.output: A source inventory and a clear reporting question.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Agree what the measures mean.
stages.body: For the first view, revenue minus direct costs is gross profit. Gross margin is gross profit divided by revenue. We agree the date range, filters and exclusions, alongside access and Microsoft sharing requirements.
stages.output: A reporting scope, measure definitions and sharing requirements.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Build a view your team can investigate.
stages.body: A first report puts sales beside costs, then lets the team compare channels. You review the layout with the questions you ask in a real meeting, rather than approving charts in isolation.
stages.output: A reviewable report and an agreed data model.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Reconcile the view with the records.
stages.body: We check totals, channel filters and refresh behaviour against known inputs. Missing costs should be visible; they should not quietly become zero and make the margin look better.
stages.output: Reconciliation checks and visible data-quality exceptions.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Explain the numbers and the refresh.
stages.body: The handover covers measure definitions, source limitations, refresh ownership and access. The team can see where a number comes from and what to check when an input changes.
stages.output: A definitions guide, refresh instructions and clear ownership.

tests.label: All channels
tests.reason: Both channel totals reconcile to the combined view.

tests.label: Online only
tests.reason: The filter changes the source records and the displayed totals.

tests.label: Missing cost
tests.reason: Review the missing input before treating the profit as dependable.

handover.title: Measure dictionary
handover.body: Revenue, direct costs, gross profit and margin, with the agreed exclusions.

handover.title: Refresh & access
handover.body: Source locations, refresh ownership, permissions and licensing requirements.

handover.title: A change in the data
handover.body: How to identify a failed refresh or a changed source column and raise it for review.
